title.en: The Mental Health Crisis on Campus

source.note: No workbook sheet exists for this mission. Authored from scratch per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md. Sensitive topic: informative and supportive framing, no graphic detail, always point toward help-seeking.

stages.source_description: Part 1: Introduction (Slides 1-3: hook noticing the people around you, SDG 3 covers mental health, campus life beneath the surface)

title.en: SDG 3 Means More Than the Body

stages.source_description: Part 2: Problem (Slides 4-6: the scale of depressive tendency among university students, where the pressure comes from, the youth mortality figures that make this urgent)
stages.language_pattern: present progressive for trends / this causes ...

stages.source_description: Part 3: Achievements (Slides 7-9: the counselor-ratio law finally changes, the 1925 hotline, psychological leave now exists on paper)
Part 4: Solutions (Slides 10-12: hiring enough counselors, making help easier to reach, campus-wide prevention instead of waiting for crisis)

title.en: Instead of Waiting for a Crisis

stages.source_description: Part 5: Implications (Slides 13-16: one continuous tension — a law that outruns its budget, access that is not the same as trust, a leave nobody takes, and why both structural and cultural fixes are needed together)

title.en: If the Law Outruns the Budget
title.zh: 如果法規跑在預算前面

title.en: Access Is Not the Same as Trust

stages.source_description: Part 6: Call to action (Slides 17-20: summary of progress and gaps, students do not need a perfect system, learn the signs and the number, reaching out is not weakness)

title.en: Progress, and What It Is Missing
You Do Not Need a Perfect System
title.zh: 你不需要一個完美的系統

title.en: Learn the Signs, Say the Number
